Hi GGJJ,

I will post the chart step-by-step so you can see the entire mental process behind the trade Hopefully it will clear things up, but if not, please don't hesitate to ask more questions. If you find a flaw in my analysis please feel free to challenge me!

Step 1:

Find a swap zone by looking for well formed & tested FL's.

Box A: Holds Price Up (Buyer Control) Box B: Holds Price Down (Seller Control)

Since i am considering a short trade, I need to make sure the last pocket of buy LQ has been absorbed. If there are unfilled buy orders lurking near my short entry I risk getting stopped out.

Step 2: I track PA as it develops between Box A and Box B. I am on the lookout for clean orders (FOF). My definition of clean orders/FOF is where institutional money artificially pushes price in the wrong direction to trap LQ to fill their positions. I need to see evidence of this happening or I can't justify taking a trade. Since I am looking for a sell trade, I am looking for a bull trap.

In this case, a bull trap does occur. It happens when price breaks the top line of Box "B" and fakes out to Box "A". This RBD FO makes me very interested in looking for a sell opportunity. Here is the chart showing the RBD:

Now that I have established a RBD FO has occurred in the right spot, I must draw the following boxes:

- Where does price break the top of Box B? Please refer to FL 1 on the chart below. - Where does price break the low of FL 1? Please refer to FL 2 on the chart below. 

At this stage, I have the major 4 boxes drawn in the right spot (within the scope of a swap zone). My entry short will happen somewhere inside FL 2, but I need to refine the entry before setting an order.

I will refine the entry by drawing the important LTF decision points and LTF swap zones within FL 1 and FL 2. I am looking for the exact spot where sellers took control of the market. I want to find the origin of that fresh bearish LQ.

Hey Hansma,

It is good to hear from you

This way of looking at the market is still pretty new to me.. but I am looking specifically for a swap zone to start the analysis. The swap zone has to include a FL that holds price up, and a FL that holds price down (I think the terminology is LFL and UFL). If drawn correctly, this should create space between these FL's. It is in this 'space' that I want to see a FO occur.

I mark all of these zones as they form...then I start looking closer to see if there is an opportunity to make a trade. I treat each UFL/LFL combination as a 'system'.

Here is a drawing:

There isn't always space between the FL's, but if there is not space, then there is always an overlap. Here is a drawing that shows overlap, but no 'open space'.

I haven't done enough testing to find out which scenario is better, but so far, I prefer the situation where there is space between the two (usually you can see a very LTF kink in the space). The key is the FO... I want to see 'clean orders' in the form of a false move to trap LQ on the wrong side. It is the FO that occurs between the two FL's that form the swap zone that seems to clear out all residual LQ..making a bounce trade perfect.

If the FO forms and clean orders are left behind, I can trade along side the IT's when they square up their positions. It is the 'squaring up' that causes the bounce.

There are some exceptions to this.. most notably situations that incorporate compression. Compression creates atypical PA and usually I set my order just at the beginning of compression (or at the very least I will place my stop beyond the compression area). When I get stopped out using this method it is almost always because I misread compression.

Looking at your example on AUD-USD, I didn't quite see the swap zone. I do see your methodology however, and I think you are on the right track.

I formulated this way of looking at the market after revisiting Salivan's trades... he regularly took trades at the last possible pocket of supply/demand near a swap zone. It almost always happened near a FO/trick. I am curious if other traders see the same opportunity as I do!

Thanks for stopping by my journal!

GGJJ wrote: Hi H, Regarding your last pocket of LQ, i would like to understand more. Here is my question.

Hi GGJJ,

Not entirely sure if I am correct, but the way I understand the 'last pocket of orders' is being the last place where buyers/seller took control of the market. There are two important pieces of information:

1. The decision to FO 2. the FTR/FL that forms after the engulf of the decision to FO.

The FTR/FL that forms after the engulf of the decision to FO is the last place where sell orders took control of the market, following the FO. When price returns to that last pocket of LQ, price bounces. That is also where price returns to 'square up' after the trick occurs ($$$ is spent to move the market in the wrong direction, and those who invest in this false move need to eventually exit their position, as it remains a constant drag on their balance sheet until the position is closed.

This is my understanding of why this 'last pocket' of LQ is so important.

Here is a basic drawing:

Specifically for the AUD-USD trade, the decision to FO is drawn, and the engulf of the Decision to FO is also drawn. That FTR/FL is where I took the trade. In my opinion, the 'last pocket' is the FL labeled 'X" below. Technically, you could have chosen the first red box, or either of the purple boxes as the 'decision to FO' and you would still end up with the same FL "X". It is in the FL "X" that price bounces.
